source.title: Explicitizing an Implicit Bias of the Frequency Principle in Two-layer Neural Networks
source.authors: Yaoyu Zhang; Zhi-Qin John Xu; Tao Luo; Zheng Ma

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports an experiment relating a measured property of the target function, its FP-norm, to test error in trained two-layer ReLU networks. This is a different measure and setting from the mapped versions, but directly tests whether a network property tracks generalization error.
record.gate_note: The paper's interpolation and LFP-versus-network approximation results concern fitting synthetic training data and do not report the mapped claim's natural-label generalization outcomes. The test-error-versus-target-frequency experiment does measure test error and FP-norm; cited results about random labels and parity are not this paper's own results.
record.test_reason: The study measures target-function FP-norm versus sinusoidal regression test error, which tests none of V1–V8. Its width sweeps measure agreement between neural-network outputs and its LFP model, not held-out error against target labels. Its discussion of random-label generalization explains cited findings without independently testing V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. More precisely, the authors derive an FP-norm-dependent generalization upper bound for the constrained LFP model and report a corresponding empirical association in a wide two-layer ReLU network. An increasing upper bound alone does not establish increasing actual error.
record.recipe_differences: Two-layer ReLU networks on synthetic sinusoidal regression data, with Adam and full-batch training; the paper studies a frequency-based implicit bias rather than the mapped interventions or comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported experiment varies target frequency; the text reports test error and FP-norm as functions of frequency but gives no further condition-specific values in prose.

fits_no_version.finding: Across sinusoidal target frequencies, a 5000-hidden-neuron ReLU network trained on 20 samples to training MSE below 10^-6 shows larger test error with larger target-function FP-norm.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Target-function FP-norm tracks test error in the tested sinusoidal regression setting.

record.problems: The experiment is reported through Figure 3 without numeric values or uncertainty estimates in the text. The results concern a single sinusoidal regression setup and do not test the mapped versions directly.

untested.parts: No paired random-label fitting and natural-label held-out accuracy experiments; the random-label discussion interprets prior findings.
No held-out target-error sweep beyond the width required for interpolation; width-dependent LFP approximation error measures a different quantity.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison under controlled tuning.
No magnitude-aware weight perturbations, sharpness measurement, or ranking of generalization gaps against alternative measures.
No memorization-based example removal and retraining comparison.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict applies to V1–V8. Figure 3 supplies a qualitative association without uncertainty estimates; the supplied text does not support precise curve values.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting or natural-label held-out performance comparison.
No test-error sweep over widths beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or other gap-ranking measure is tested.

rows.subject: ReLU-NN of width 1-5000-1
rows.stage_stated: trained until training MSE loss was smaller than 10^-6
rows.operation_detail: Measured test error and target-function FP-norm across target frequencies.
rows.measure: Test loss as a function of target frequency and target-function FP-norm.
rows.value: A larger FP-norm of the target function is related to a larger test error.
rows.note: The text describes the relationship but gives no numeric values or uncertainty for the curve.
rows.check: The reported FP-norm/test-error association is correctly extracted, but cannot establish any mapped version. In particular, FP-norm of the target function is not magnitude-aware weight sharpness, and test loss is not a comparison of generalization-gap rankings. Add Xavier normal initialization, antisymmetrical initialization, and learning rate 10^-4 to the conditions.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
